title: Keep the Batch45 strict delete as a product-owned pool-release proof
outcome: The process-follower strict workspace deletion detects regressions in IndexManager-owned SQLite pool release instead of clearing those pools from the test.
acceptance: Focused and full Windows gates pass with no codenav-45-process-follower residual.
ShutdownAsync remains responsible for writer pool release and the retry-free delete still asserts workspace absence.
WindowsFollowerKeepsServingCommittedStateAcrossWriterExitAndSuccessorRebuild does not call ClearIndexPools before its strict root deletion when all pools are product-owned.
